{{Legend0|#D3D3D3|No election}} }} [[Elections in the United States#State elections|Gubernatorial elections]] were held in the United States on November 4, 2025, in [[New Jersey]] and [[Virginia]]. Both states had last elected governors in [[2021 United States gubernatorial elections|2021]], with both incumbents being ineligible to seek re-election due to term limits in their respective state constitutions.{{Cite web|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=2021-11-03|title=Phil Murphy narrowly reelected governor in New Jersey, defeating Republican Jack Ciattarelli|url=https://6abc.com/11193888/|access-date=2021-11-03|website=6abc Philadelphia|language=en}}{{Cite web|title=Term Limits on Governor|url=https://www.termlimits.com/governor_termlimits/|access-date=2021-11-03|work=U.S. Term Limits}} In the [[2024 United States presidential election]], both states voted for Democratic nominee [[Kamala Harris]] by a 5-6% margin.{{cite web |last1=Jamerson |first1=Joshua |title=New Jersey and Virginia Are Typically Blue States—but They Got Bluer |url=https://www.wsj.com/livecoverage/election-day-2025/card/new-jersey-and-virginia-are-typically-blue-states-but-they-got-bluer-bXyDOYfWEzLQKpIBYhTR?gaa_at=eafs&gaa_n=AWEtsqeZdeMDwv70wu73zsE3x7hnqS25E-IqwxCQu4DKvAFZrEdyecQ1i62mwVRJ7QA%3D&gaa_ts=6910e416&gaa_sig=QyZgpgSaN2RhXnDjwt7qhR6UPyWgHU2ynW9gFCOrwjmQ9MGDDz2ArBhWtr_00bdq_vnpKO9ZcpJCiD883Bazkw%3D%3D |publisher=Wall Street Journal |access-date=9 November 2025}} New Jersey in particular had a large swing to the right in [[2024 United States presidential election in New Jersey|2024]], with [[Donald Trump]] losing the state by only 6%, and had narrowly re-elected Democrat [[Phil Murphy]] in [[2021 New Jersey gubernatorial election|2021]], leading some to expect a close race.{{cite web |last1=Friedman |first1=Matt |last2=Han |first2=Daniel |title=New Jersey might be a swing state now |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2024/11/06/new-jersey-swing-state-red-00187965 |publisher=Politico |access-date=9 November 2025}}{{cite web |last1=Catalini |first1=Mike |last2=Peoples |first2=Steve |title=Democrats wary support may be sliding among typically loyal voters in New Jersey governor's race |url=https://apnews.com/article/new-jersey-governor-ciattarelli-sherrill-trump-812eb76552a8e6f8605d5d5bfbaccf0a |publisher=AP News |access-date=9 November 2025}} Ultimately, Democratic nominees [[Mikie Sherrill]] and [[Abigail Spanberger]] won their races in New Jersey and Virginia, respectively, by wide margins and outperformed Harris.{{cite web |last1=Oliphant |first1=James |title=Takeaways from US election night 2025 |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/us/takeaways-us-election-night-2025-2025-11-05/ |publisher=Reuters |access-date=9 November 2025}} This is the first time since [[1985 United States gubernatorial elections|1985]] where every race in this cycle of governorships was decided by double digits. == Partisan composition == Heading into the election, there were 27 Republican governors and 23 Democratic governors in the United States. The gubernatorial seats were up in the moderately blue states of Virginia and New Jersey where there was one Republican and one Democratic seat. Republicans were defending one governorship in a state that [[Kamala Harris]] won in 2024 (Virginia). Democrats were defending one governorship in a state that Harris won (New Jersey). ==Election predictions== Several sites and individuals publish predictions of competitive seats. These predictions looked at factors such as the strength of the [[incumbent]] (if the incumbent is running for re-election), the strength of the candidates, and the partisan leanings of the state (reflected in part by the state's [[Cook Partisan Voting Index]] rating). The predictions assigned ratings to each seat, with the rating indicating a party's predicted advantage in winning that seat. Most election predictors use: * "tossup": no advantage * "tilt" (used by some predictors): advantage that is not quite as strong as "lean" * "lean": slight advantage * "likely": significant, but surmountable, advantage * "safe" or "solid": near-certain chance of victory {|class="wikitable sortable" |- valign=bottom ! He was [[Term limits in the United States|term-limited]] by the [[New Jersey Constitution]] and couldn't seek re-election for a third consecutive term. [[Jersey City, New Jersey|Jersey City]] [[Mayor of Jersey City, New Jersey|mayor]] [[Steven Fulop]], former [[New Jersey Senate]] president [[Stephen Sweeney]], U.S. Representatives [[Josh Gottheimer]] and [[Mikie Sherrill]], and [[Newark, New Jersey|Newark]] [[Mayor of Newark, New Jersey|mayor]] [[Ras Baraka]] ran for the Democratic nomination.{{cite web|url=https://newjerseyglobe.com/governor/fulop-announces-bid-for-governor-in-2025/|title=Fulop announces bid for Governor in 2025|last=Wildstein|first=David|date=April 11, 2023|access-date=April 11, 2023|work=[[New Jersey Globe]]}}{{cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2023/12/11/steve-sweeney-new-jersey-governors-race-00131060|title=Sweeney enters NJ governor’s race after upset loss as Senate president|last=Racioppi|first=Dustin|date=December 11, 2023|access-date=December 11, 2023|work=Politico}}{{cite web|url=https://newjerseyglobe.com/governor/baraka-says-hell-run-for-governor-in-2025/|title=Baraka Says He’ll Run For Governor In 2025|last=Wildstein|first=David|date=February 19, 2024|access-date=February 19, 2024|work=[[New Jersey Globe]]}}{{cite web|title=Rep. Former state Assemblyman [[Jack Ciattarelli]], who was the Republican nominee in [[2021 New Jersey gubernatorial election|2021]], was the Republican nominee. Sherrill won the election, becoming the second female governor of New Jersey when several media outlets called the race for her over Ciattarelli on November 4, 2025.{{Cite news |last=Fernandez |first=Madison |date=November 4, 2025 |title=Sherrill Wins NJ gov |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/11/04/mikie-sherrill-new-jersey-governor-wins-00635466 |url-status=live |access-date=November 17, 2025 |work=[[Politico]]}}{{Cite news |date=November 4, 2025 |title=AP Race Call: Democrat Mikie Sherrill elected NJ governor over Trump-backed Jack Ciattarelli |url=https://apnews.com/article/new-jersey-nj-governor-bf74d0bf8607149b54930b3aff6236bb |url-status=live |access-date=November 17, 2025 |work=[[Associated Press]]}}{{Cite news |last=Saenz |first=Arlette |date=November 4, 2025 |title=Democrat Mikie Sherrill wins New Jersey governor’s race |url=https://www.cnn.com/2025/11/04/politics/nj-governor-mikie-sherrill-wins |url-status=live |access-date=November 17, 2025 |work=[[CNN]]}} In addition, she won three consecutive terms for her party for the first time in the state since 1961. '''Tie:''' {{legend0|#D2B1D9|40–50%}} {{legend0|#AE8BB1|50%}} | title = [[Governor of New Jersey|Governor]] | before_election = [[Phil Murphy]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Mikie Sherrill]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{Elections in New Jersey sidebar}} The '''2025 New Jersey gubernatorial election''' was held on November 4, 2025, to elect the [[governor of New Jersey]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] U.S. representative [[Mikie Sherrill]] defeated [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] former nominee [[Jack Ciattarelli]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/11/04/us/elections/results-new-jersey-governor.html|title=New Jersey Governor Election Results 2025: Mikie Sherrill Wins|work=The New York Times|date=November 4, 2025|via=NYTimes.com|access-date=November 5, 2025|archive-date=November 5, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251105170227/https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/11/04/us/elections/results-new-jersey-governor.html|url-status=live}}{{cite web |last1=Simko |first1=Tyler |last2=Khanna |first2=Kabir |title=Sherrill wins New Jersey governor's race |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/mikie-sherrill-landslide-new-jersey-high-turnout-analysis/ |publisher=CBS News |access-date=5 November 2025 |archive-date=November 6, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251106031953/https://www.cbsnews.com/news/mikie-sherrill-landslide-new-jersey-high-turnout-analysis/ |url-status=live }}{{cite web|last1=Sherman|first1=Ted|title=A broken crystal ball? Why the polls in the Sherrill landslide victory got it wrong again.|url=https://www.nj.com/politics/2025/11/a-broken-crystal-ball-why-the-polls-in-the-sherrill-landslide-victory-got-it-wrong-again.html|publisher=NJ.com|access-date=6 November 2025|archive-date=November 7, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251107032136/https://www.nj.com/politics/2025/11/a-broken-crystal-ball-why-the-polls-in-the-sherrill-landslide-victory-got-it-wrong-again.html|url-status=live}} Sherrill succeeded Democratic incumbent [[Phil Murphy]], who was [[Term limits in the United States|term-limited]] and thus ineligible to seek a third term. [[Primary elections]] were held on June 10, 2025.{{Cite web |date=2025-06-10 |title=Live updates: New Jersey governor, Atlantic City mayor are key races in NJ primary |url=https://www.nbcphiladelphia.com/news/politics/live-updates-new-jersey-primary-election-governor-atlantic-city-mayor/4206045/ |access-date=2025-11-05 |website=NBC10 Philadelphia |language=en-US |archive-date=October 31, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251031180030/https://www.nbcphiladelphia.com/news/politics/live-updates-new-jersey-primary-election-governor-atlantic-city-mayor/4206045/ |url-status=live }} Sherrill won the Democratic nomination with 34% of the vote over a field of candidates that included Newark mayor [[Ras Baraka]] and Jersey City mayor [[Steven Fulop]]. Ciattarelli, the Republican nominee in [[2021 New Jersey gubernatorial election|2021]], won his second consecutive nomination with almost 68% of the vote over radio talk show host [[Bill Spadea]]. After strong Republican performances in the state in [[2021 New Jersey gubernatorial election|2021]] and [[2024 United States presidential election in New Jersey|2024]], many analysts expected a close race. Some polls suggested the election was a toss-up.{{cite web | title = New Jersey Democrats worry support sliding in governor′s race | website = AP News | date = September 30, 2025 | url = https://apnews.com/article/new-jersey-governor-ciattarelli-sherrill-trump-812eb76552a8e6f8605d5d5bfbaccf0a | accessdate = November 5, 2025 }}{{cite web | last = Vakil | first = Caroline | title = Sherrill, Ciattarelli in tight race for N.J. governor | website = The Hill | date = October 30, 2025 | url =https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5579199-sherrill-ciattarelli-nj-governor| accessdate = November 5, 2025}} However, Sherrill outperformed expectations and won with a decisive 14.36% margin of victory, slightly larger than Murphy's 14.14% margin in [[2017 New Jersey gubernatorial election|2017]]. This election was the widest Democratic margin since [[2001 New Jersey gubernatorial election|2001]], and the highest vote share for a Democratic nominee since [[1989 New Jersey gubernatorial election|1989]]. Sherrill was the first Democratic gubernatorial candidate to win Morris County since [[1973 New Jersey gubernatorial election|1973]]. Sherrill also lost [[Hunterdon County, New Jersey|Hunterdon County]] by single digits, which is the narrowest Republican margin since [[1977 New Jersey gubernatorial election|1977]].{{cite web |url=http://www.state.nj.us/state/elections/1920-1970-results/1973-general-election.pdf |title=Votes Cast for the Office of Governor of the State of New Jersey |publisher=[[Secretary of State of New Jersey]] |year=1973 |access-date=August 22, 2015 |archive-date=December 15, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141215234116/http://www.state.nj.us/state/elections/1920-1970-results/1973-general-election.pdf |url-status=live }}{{cite web |url=http://www.state.nj.us/state/elections/1920-1970-results/1977-general-election.pdf |title=Votes Cast for the Office of Governor of the State of New Jersey |publisher=[[Secretary of State of New Jersey]] |year=1977 |access-date=August 21, 2015 |archive-date=September 10, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150910050306/http://www.state.nj.us/state/elections/1920-1970-results/1977-general-election.pdf |url-status=dead }} Both Sherrill and Ciattarelli obtained the most votes cast in any New Jersey gubernatorial election, and this election had the highest turnout since [[1997 New Jersey gubernatorial election|1997]].{{Cite news|date=November 14, 2025|title=N.J. just experienced its most dramatic voter surge in decades. See the surprising numbers.|url=https://www.nj.com/politics/2025/11/nj-just-experienced-its-most-dramatic-voter-surge-in-decades-see-the-surprising-numbers.html|access-date=November 21, 2025|website=NJ.com|archive-date=November 15, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251115142857/https://www.nj.com/politics/2025/11/nj-just-experienced-its-most-dramatic-voter-surge-in-decades-see-the-surprising-numbers.html|url-status=live}} Sherrill was sworn in as the 57th governor of New Jersey on January 20, 2026. This election was considered to be an indicator of the popularity of [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|Donald Trump's second presidency]] in the state. Until [[2021 New Jersey gubernatorial election|2021]], New Jersey had elected a governor of the opposite party of the sitting [[president of the United States]] in every election since [[1989 New Jersey gubernatorial election|1989]].{{cite news |title=2021 NJ Election: Democratic Incumbent Phil Murphy Wins 2nd Term As Governor, Beating Republican Jack Ciattarelli - CBS Philadelphia |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/philadelphia/news/phil-murphy-wins-second-term-new-jersey-governor/ |access-date=October 19, 2025 |work=CBS News |date=November 4, 2021 |archive-date=January 18, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260118150848/https://www.cbsnews.com/philadelphia/news/phil-murphy-wins-second-term-new-jersey-governor/ |url-status=live }} Until this election, New Jersey had not elected the same party to the governor's office for more than two consecutive terms since [[1961 New Jersey gubernatorial election|1961]].{{cite web | url=https://www.nj.com/politics/2025/04/jack-ciattarelli-will-be-njs-next-governor-unless-trump-screws-him.html | title=Jack Ciattarelli will be N.J.'s next governor (Unless Trump screws him) | date=April 10, 2025 | access-date=May 29, 2025 | archive-date=May 15, 2025 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250515214359/https://www.nj.com/politics/2025/04/jack-ciattarelli-will-be-njs-next-governor-unless-trump-screws-him.html | url-status=live }} In October 2025, the Trump administration announced that the [[United States Department of Justice|Department of Justice]] would deploy election monitors to polling sites in California and New Jersey ahead of the November 4 elections. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] former congresswoman [[Abigail Spanberger]] defeated [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] lieutenant governor [[Winsome Earle-Sears]]. Spanberger succeeded Republican incumbent [[Glenn Youngkin]], who was [[Term limits in the United States|term-limited]] and ineligible to seek a second consecutive term. Earle-Sears and Spanberger ran unopposed in their respective party primaries. In April 2025, they were confirmed as the major party nominees.{{cite news|last=Bianco|first=Ali|date=April 5, 2025|title=Virginia's bellwether governor race is set|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/04/05/virginia-governor-race-candidates-00006980|access-date=April 5, 2025|website=[[Politico]]}} The central issues of the campaign were the economy and [[United States affordability crisis|affordability]], which included the federal layoffs from the [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]]. [[Transgender rights in the United States|Transgender rights]] and political rhetoric were secondary issues.{{Cite web |last=Manchester |first=Julie |date=September 30, 2025 |title=Spanberger sees |access-date=December 12, 2025 |work=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]]}} [[President Donald Trump]]'s approval and perceived performance on the economy, healthcare, immigration, and other issues were viewed as contributing factors for Earle-Sears's loss.{{Cite news |last=Sanders & Boak |first=Linley & Josh |date=November 5, 2025 |title=Tuesday's races were a quiet rebuke of Trump for many |access-date=December 7, 2025 |work=[[Associated Press]]}} Spanberger won the general election by 15.36%—the largest gubernatorial percentage margin since [[2009 Virginia gubernatorial election|2009]]. Democrats flipped all three statewide executive offices and [[2025 Virginia House of Delegates election|expanded]] their majority in the [[Virginia House of Delegates|House of Delegates]], creating a Democratic trifecta in Virginia's government for the first time since [[2019 Virginia elections|2019]].{{Cite news|last=Schmidt|first=Markus|date=November 4, 2025|title=Blue wave rebuilds the House: |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/dc-md-va/2026/01/17/spanberger-inauguration-virginia-governor/ |access-date=January 17, 2026 |work=[[The Washington Post]]}} == Background == In the [[2021 Virginia gubernatorial election|2021 gubernatorial election]], Youngkin defeated former governor [[Terry McAuliffe]] by two points, after [[Joe Biden]] won the state in [[2020 United States presidential election in Virginia|2020]] by 10 points. The central issues of the election were the economy and education. In that election, Republicans flipped the three statewide executive offices and the [[Virginia House of Delegates|House of Delegates]].{{Cite web|author=270toWin Staff|date=November 1, 2021|title=Outcome of Races for Governor and House Control in Virginia Will Define Election Day 2021|url=https://www.270towin.com/news/2021/11/01/outcome-races-governor-house-delegates-control-virginia-will-define-election-day-2021_1259.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241106185710/https://www.270towin.com/news/2021/11/01/outcome-races-governor-house-delegates-control-virginia-will-define-election-day-2021_1259.html|archive-date=November 6, 2024|access-date=January 4, 2026|website=[[270toWin]]}} In the [[2023 Virginia elections|2023 legislative elections]], Democrats narrowly flipped the House of Delegates and maintained control of the [[Virginia Senate|Senate]].{{cite news|last=Kronzer|first=Jessica|date=November 7, 2023|title=Democrats sweep Virginia elections to take control of General Assembly|url=https://wtop.com/local-politics-elections-news/2023/11/tallying-is-underway-which-party-will-take-hold-of-virginias-general-assembly/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240524081231/https://wtop.com/local-politics-elections-news/2023/11/democrats-sweep-virginia-elections-to-take-control-of-general-assembly/|archive-date=May 24, 2024|access-date=November 8, 2023 |publisher=[[WTOP News]]}} Youngkin, who had a 20% net approval, was ineligible to run for re-election to a second consecutive term due to [[Term limits in the United States|term limits]] set in the [[Virginia Constitution]].{{cite web|last=Kramer|first=Bill|date=April 22, 2025|title=Here's What America Thinks of Its Governors (Governors Ranked by Approval Rating)|url=https://www.multistate.us/insider/2025/4/22/heres-what-america-thinks-of-its-governors-governors-ranked-by-approval-rating|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251213224903/https://www.multistate.us/insider/2025/4/22/heres-what-america-thinks-of-its-governors-governors-ranked-by-approval-rating|archive-date=December 13, 2025|access-date=May 16, 2026|website=MultiState}} In the 2024 presidential election, Republican former president Donald Trump was re-elected, which Democrats hoped would energize their voter base in the off-year elections. Trump's personal popularity and voters' position on the economy were viewed as crucial to which party would win the election.{{Cite news|last=Schmidt|first=Markus|date=November 20, 2024|title=Trump's victory sets the stage for high-stakes Virginia elections in 2025|url=https://virginiamercury.com/2024/11/20/trumps-victory-sets-the-stage-for-high-stakes-virginia-elections-in-2025/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250503125159/https://virginiamercury.com/2024/11/20/trumps-victory-sets-the-stage-for-high-stakes-virginia-elections-in-2025/|archive-date=May 3, 2025|access-date=January 9, 2026|work=[[Virginia Mercury]]}} In January 2025, Trump and [[Elon Musk]] introduced the [[Department of Government Efficiency]].{{Efn|Commonly referred to as DOGE}} DOGE laid off thousands of federal workers, mainly in [[Northern Virginia]] and [[Hampton Roads]], where 140,000 federal workers resided.{{Cite web|last=Mutnick|first=Ally|date=February 12, 2025|title=How Trump's assault on bureaucracy could rock Virginia elections|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/02/12/trump-democrats-virginia-bureacracy-00203845|access-date=February 12, 2025|website=[[Politico]]}} Due to Virginia's [[Red states and blue states|Democratic]] lean, the state was viewed as a likely gubernatorial pickup for Democrats while national circumstances were unfavorable for Republicans.{{Cite web|last=Phillips|first=Logan|title=2025-2026 Governor Forecast|url=https://www.racetothewh.com/governor/26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250705193136/https://www.racetothewh.com/governor/26|archive-date=July 5, 2025|access-date=January 4, 2026|website=Race To The White House}} With the exception of [[2013 Virginia gubernatorial election|2013]], Virginia has not elected a governor from the same party as the incumbent president since [[1977 Virginia gubernatorial election|1977]].{{Cite web|last=McDonald|first=Christopher J.|date=November 6, 2024|title=2024 Virginia Election Recap|url=https://www.williamsmullen.com/insights/news/legal-news/2024-virginia-election-recap|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260120202134/https://www.williamsmullen.com/insights/news/legal-news/2024-virginia-election-recap|archive-date=January "Congressman Wittman is looking forward to serving his constituents in the 119th Congress and running for re-election to Congress in 2026." |author=Andrew Solender |date=December 4, 2024}} ===Campaign=== On September 4, 2024, Winsome Earle-Sears declared her candidacy for governor. She was criticized by attorney general [[Jason Miyares]], who was viewed as a potential candidate, for making her announcement ahead of the 2024 elections.{{Cite news |last=Vozzella |first=Laura |last2=Schneider |first2=Gregory S. |date=September 5, 2024 |title=Virginia Lt. Gov. Winsome Earle-Sears announces her candidacy for governor |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/dc-md-va/2024/09/05/virginia-lt-gov-winsome-earle-sears-announces-her-candidacy-governor/ |url-access=subscription |access-date=December 19, 2025 |work=[[The Washington Post]]}} After the 2024 elections, Miyares declined to run for governor, with Earle-Sears being described as the presumptive nominee.{{cite web |last1=Yancey |first1=Dwayne |date=November 18, 2024 |title=Miyares to seek re-election; 2025 governor's race now appears set |url=https://cardinalnews.org/2024/11/18/miyares-to-see-re-election-2025-governors-race-now-appears-set/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250120035904/https://cardinalnews.org/2024/11/18/miyares-to-see-re-election-2025-governors-race-now-appears-set/ |archive-date=January 20, 2025 |access-date=February 28, 2025 |website=Cardinal News}} On February 27, former state senator [[Amanda Chase]] and former state delegate [[Dave LaRock]] entered the primary in opposition to Earle-Sears. They associated themselves with President Trump and criticized Earle-Sears's previous comments about him. Despite the newfound opposition, Earle-Sears was still viewed as the favorite in the primary.{{Cite web |last1=Schmidt |first1=Markus |date=February 27, 2025 |title=Earle-Sears' uncontested run ends as rivals enter Virginia GOP primary for governor |url=https://virginiamercury.com/2025/02/27/earle-sears-uncontested-run-ends-as-rivals-enter-virginia-gop-primary-for-governor/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260122000638/https://virginiamercury.com/2025/02/27/earle-sears-uncontested-run-ends-as-rivals-enter-virginia-gop-primary-for-governor/ |archive-date=January 22, 2026 |access-date=February 28, 2025 |website=[[Virginia Mercury]]}}{{Cite web |last1=Englander |first1=Tyler |date=February 27, 2025 |title=Is Lieutenant Gov. |archive-date=February 22, 2026 |access-date=October 13, 2025 |website=[[WAVY.com]]}} ==General election== ===Campaign=== [[File:Jay Jones, Ghazala Hashmi and Abigail Spanberger at a bus rally in Fairfax City.jpg|thumb|[[Ghazala Hashmi]] speaking at a bus rally in [[Fairfax, Virginia|Fairfax]] with [[Jay Jones]] and Spanberger]] [[File:Lt Gov Winsome Earle-Sears (92ce22f0-6052-4c8b-a303-201e80a2c2ca).JPG|thumb|Winsome Earle-Sears speaking at [[Petersburg National Battlefield]]]] This was the first gubernatorial election in the state's history in which both major party nominees were women.{{Cite news |last=Moreno |first=Sabrina |date=April 8, 2025 |title=Virginia set to elect first woman governor in 2025 race |url=https://www.axios.com/local/richmond/2025/04/08/virginia-first-woman-governor-2025 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251208224530/https://www.axios.com/local/richmond/2025/04/08/virginia-first-woman-governor-2025 |archive-date=December 8, 2025 |access-date=January 19, 2026 |work=[[Axios (website)|Axios]]}} President Trump instated [[Tariffs in the second Trump administration|tariffs]] on other nations including [[Canada]] and [[China]]. The tariffs were expected to increase prices on consumer goods from companies who relied on foreign imports. Spanberger disagreed with the tariffs and said they were "... a massive tax hike on Virginians — plain and simple."{{Cite news |last=Guerra |first=Shirleen |date=April 7, 2025 |title=Tariffs spark backlash in Virginia over economic impact |url=https://www.thecentersquare.com/virginia/article_59132470-26c8-463c-ab38-596f51c7f035.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250407203439/https://www.thecentersquare.com/virginia/article_59132470-26c8-463c-ab38-596f51c7f035.html |archive-date=April 7, 2025 |access-date=February 8, 2026 |work=[[The Center Square]]}} Virginia Democrats highlighted Earle-Sears's conservative positions on social issues and support for tariffs.{{Cite news |last=Booker |first=Brakkton |last2=Crampton |first2=Liz |last3=Jacobs |first3=Ben |date=May 20, 2025 |title=Virginia Republicans worry about their gubernatorial candidate who invoked slavery when criticizing DEI |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/05/19/virginia-gop-winsome-earle-sears-worries-00357698 |access-date=February 7, 2026 |work=[[Politico]]}} After the June primaries, the economy emerged as the main issue for both campaigns. Spanberger's campaign message was focused on affordability: she continued to oppose federal layoffs and tariffs from the Trump administration. Earle-Sears pledged to continue Youngkin's economic policies.{{Cite news |last=McNamara |first=Nick |date=July 23, 2025 |title=Economic issues at the forefront for Spanberger, Earle-Sears |url=https://www.whro.org/virginia-government/2025-07-23/economic-issues-at-the-forefront-for-spanberger-earle-sears |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250724142712/https://www.whro.org/virginia-government/2025-07-23/economic-issues-at-the-forefront-for-spanberger-earle-sears |archive-date=July 24, 2025 |access-date=February 15, 2026 |work=WHRO public media}} After Earle-Sears replaced her campaign manager, there were internal concerns from the [[Republican Party of Virginia|Virginia Republican Party]] over how her campaign was managed. By July, Spanberger significantly outraised Earle-Sears, while there was lack of Republican investment in the race compared to [[2021 Virginia gubernatorial election|2021]].{{Cite news |last=Manchester |first=Julia |date=July 23, 2025 |title=Virginia Republicans sound alarm over governor's race: 'It's a disaster' |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5413919-earle-sears-campaign-struggles-continue/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250723125719/https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5413919-earle-sears-campaign-struggles-continue/ |archive-date=July 23, 2025 |access-date=February 18, 2026 |work=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]}}{{Cite news |last=Martin |first=Jonathan |date=July 23, 2025 |title=Republicans Are Panicking Over the Virginia Governor's Race |url=https://www.politico.com/news/magazine/2025/07/23/virginia-governors-race-republicans-jonathan-martin-column-00468311 |access-date=February 18, 2026 |work=[[Politico]]}} Earle-Sears's statements on federal workers throughout the campaign were criticized as "self-inflicted wounds" and supportive of President Trump's DOGE cuts.{{Cite news |last=Yancey |first=Dwayne |date=August 7, 2025 |title=Earle-Sears could learn from Reid how to talk about federal job cuts |url=https://cardinalnews.org/2025/08/07/earle-sears-could-learn-from-reid-how-to-talk-about-federal-job-cuts/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250807081714/https://cardinalnews.org/2025/08/07/earle-sears-could-learn-from-reid-how-to-talk-about-federal-job-cuts/ |archive-date=August 7, 2025 |access-date=February 20, 2026 |work=Cardinal News}} Earle-Sears began to focus on [[Transgender youth|transgender policies]] in Northern Virginia's schools, which mirrored Youngkin's focus on [[critical race theory]] in 2021. On August 21, Earle-Sears's speech at an [[Arlington County, Virginia|Arlington County]] School Board meeting received protests. One protest sign stated, "Hey Winsome, if trans{{Sic}} can't share your bathroom, then Blacks can't share my water fountain." The sign received media attention and condemnation from Spanberger and Earle-Sears.{{Cite news |last=Manchester |first=Julia |date=August 25, 2025 |title=Virginia GOP grows cautiously optimistic in governor's race |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5466778-virginia-republicans-optimistic-winsome-earle-sears/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250825102004/https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5466778-virginia-republicans-optimistic-winsome-earle-sears/ |archive-date=August 25, 2025 |access-date=February 19, 2026 |work=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]}} Spanberger continued to campaign on affordability issues, which remained the top issue for voters. She campaigned in [[Southwest Virginia]] and attempted to win over rural voters who voted Trump in [[2024 United States presidential election in Virginia|2024]].{{Cite web |last=Olivia |first=Diaz |date=June 7, 2025 |title=A Virginia Democrat hunts for votes in rural pockets where MAGA has strengthened its grip |url=https://www.wsls.com/news/local/2025/06/07/a-virginia-democrat-hunts-for-votes-in-rural-pockets-where-maga-has-strengthened-its-grip/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250608102720/https://www.wsls.com/news/local/2025/06/07/a-virginia-democrat-hunts-for-votes-in-rural-pockets-where-maga-has-strengthened-its-grip/ |archive-date=June 8, 2025 |access-date=March 10, 2026 |website=[[The Associated Press]]}}{{Cite web |last=Khalil |first=Jahid |date=October 7, 2025 |title=Spanberger makes play for rural voters in Virginia governor's race |url=https://www.vpm.org/elections/2025-10-07/election-2025-rural-voters-va-gov-spanberger-earle-sears-medicaid-agriculture |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251009113947/https://www.vpm.org/elections/2025-10-07/election-2025-rural-voters-va-gov-spanberger-earle-sears-medicaid-agriculture |archive-date=October 9, 2025 |access-date=March 10, 2026 |website=[[Virginia Mercury]]}} By October, Earle-Sears ran mainly on anti-transgender policies in schools. Earle-Sears ran attack ads against Spanberger which resembled the "[[Kamala is for they/them]]" ad from the [[2024 United States presidential election|2024 presidential election]]. She spent $2 million on anti-transgender and [[Woke|anti-woke]] ads, which made up a significant portion of her campaign advertisements.{{Cite news |last=Manchester |first=Julia |date=September 28, 2025 |title=Earle-Sears's focus on culture issues in Virginia risks backfiring |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5524212-earle-sears-spanberger-transgender-debate/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251005114124/https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5524212-earle-sears-spanberger-transgender-debate/ |archive-date=October 5, 2025 |access-date=February 20, 2026 |work=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]}}{{Cite web |author1=David Wright |author2=Eva McKend |date=2025-10-03 |title=Republicans double down on trans issues as a wedge with Virginia voters |url=https://www.cnn.com/2025/10/03/politics/transgender-politics-virginia-governor |access-date=2025-10-11 |website=CNN |language=en}} On October 1, a [[2025 United States federal government shutdown|federal government shutdown]] began, which further affected federal workers and became a central issue by the end of the campaign. According to several polls, the Republican Party was largely blamed for the shutdown. Both Spanberger and Earle-Sears opposed the shutdown, while Spanberger tied the shutdown to President Trump's policies on federal workers.{{Cite web |last=Edelman |first=Adam |last2=Bowman |first2=Bridget |date=October 1, 2025 |title=Government shutdown threatens to upend Virginia's race for governor |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/elections/government-shutdown-threatens-upend-virginias-race-governor-rcna234254 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251001092240/https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/elections/government-shutdown-threatens-upend-virginias-race-governor-rcna234254 |archive-date=October 1, 2025 |access-date=March 8, 2026 |website=[[NBC News]] |language=en}}{{Cite web |author1=Bailey |author2=Waddick |title=Could the federal shutdown and DOGE cuts tip Virginia's governor's race? |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2025/10/07/federal-shutdown-doge-virginia-election/86246074007/ |access-date=2025-10-08 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US |date=October 7, 2025 |first=Phillip M. |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251007145342/https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2025/10/07/federal-shutdown-doge-virginia-election/86246074007/ |archive-date=October 7, 2025 |first2=Karissa}} Political violence became another central issue to the campaign after the [[assassination of Charlie Kirk|Charlie Kirk assassination]], which Republicans hoped would energize low-turnout voters. The conservative ''[[National Review]]'' released text messages from [[Jay Jones]]—the Democratic nominee for [[2025 Virginia Attorney General election|attorney general]]—which referred to former Republican speaker [[Todd Gilbert]]: "If those guys die before me...I will go to their funerals to piss on their graves." He also stated, "Three people, two bullets. Gilbert, hitler, and pol pot. Gilbert gets two bullets to the head. Spoiler: put Gilbert in the crew with the two worst people you know and he receives both bullets every time." He reportedly fantasized about the death of Gilbert's children.{{Cite web |last=Fahlberg |first=Audrey |date=October 3, 2025 |title=Dem AG Nominee Jay Jones Fantasized About Shooting Former Virginia GOP Speaker: ‘He Receives Both Bullets' |url=https://www.nationalreview.com/news/dem-ag-nominee-jay-jones-fantasized-about-shooting-former-virginia-gop-speaker-he-receives-both-bullets/ |access-date=March 12, 2026 |website=[[National Review]]}} The text messages were criticized by President Trump, Glenn Youngkin, and other prominent Republicans officials who called for Jones to withdraw from the race. Spanberger condemned the text messages but did not call for him to withdraw from the race. Earle-Sears attempted to tie Jones to Spanberger and spent $1 million on [[Attack ad|attack ads]], which criticized Spanberger's stance on Jones' text messages. Democrats largely defended Spanberger's response to the messages, while the messages themselves received significant media attention.{{Cite web |last=Bailey |first=Phillip M. |title='Sick' texts from Democratic AG candidate could threaten Spanberger chances in Virginia |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2025/10/06/virginia-jay-jones-democrat-text-governor-race/86546279007/ |access-date=2025-10-08 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US|date=October 7, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251007050720/https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2025/10/06/virginia-jay-jones-democrat-text-governor-race/86546279007/|archive-date=October 7, 2025}}{{Cite web |last=Manchester |first=Julia |date=8 October 2025 |title=Earle-Sears places $1M ad buy in wake of Jones scandal |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5545766-virginia-gubernatorial-ad-buy/ |access-date=13 October 2025 |website=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251008203054/https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5545766-virginia-gubernatorial-ad-buy/|archive-date=October 8, 2025}}{{Cite news |last=Barthel |first=Margaret |date=October 16, 2025 |title=The two wildcards shaping the tail end of the Virginia race for governor |url=https://www.npr.org/2025/10/16/nx-s1-5575760/virginia-election-governor-2025-shutdown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251016091408/https://www.npr.org/2025/10/16/nx-s1-5575760/virginia-election-governor-2025-shutdown |archive-date=October 16, 2025 |access-date=March 11, 2026 |work=[[NPR]] |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Manchester |first=Julia |date=October 11, 2025 |title=Virginia Democrats defend Spanberger's handling of Jones text scandal |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5550374-spanberger-republican-attacks-jones-texts/ |access-date=March 11, 2026 |website=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]}} At [[James Madison University]]'s football game, one fan shouted at Earle-Sears, "Go back to Haiti." The event received condemnation from the university, and the fan was banned from the university.{{Cite web |author=|date=2025-10-21 |title=JMU responds after video of fan shouting at Winsome Earle-Sears goes viral |url=https://www.12onyourside.com/2025/10/21/jmu-responds-after-video-fan-shouting-winsome-earle-sears-goes-viral/ |access-date=2025-10-23 |website=12onyourside.com |language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251023050304/https://www.12onyourside.com/2025/10/21/jmu-responds-after-video-fan-shouting-winsome-earle-sears-goes-viral/|archive-date=October 23, 2025}} Former president [[Barack Obama]] appeared in two ads for Spanberger's campaign which highlighted abortion rights and economic issues. Obama further criticized President Trump's policies.{{Cite web |last=Bowman |first=Bridget |date=October 16, 2025 |title=Obama endorses Abigail Spanberger in Virginia's race for governor |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/elections/obama-endorses-abigail-spanberger-virginias-race-governor-rcna237915 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260102204052/https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/elections/obama-endorses-abigail-spanberger-virginias-race-governor-rcna237915 |archive-date=January 2, 2026 |access-date=March 14, 2026 |website=[[NBC News]]}} Other national figures campaigned for Spanberger, including [[Pete Buttigieg]], [[Andy Beshear]], [[Ruben Gallego]], [[Josh Shapiro]], and [[Wes Moore]].{{Cite web |last=Bowman |first=Bridget |date=October 20, 2025 |title=Potential 2028 presidential contenders hit the trail in this year's big campaigns |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/elections/potential-2028-presidential-contenders-hit-trail-years-big-campaigns-rcna238144 |access-date=March 15, 2026 |website=[[NBC News]]}}{{Cite web |last=Vakil |first=Caroline |date=October 27, 2025 |title=Gallego campaigning for Spanberger ahead of Virginia gubernatorial race |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5574899-spanberger-gallego-virginia-election/ |access-date=March 15, 2026 |website=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]}}{{Cite web |last=Harrell |first=Princess |date=October 31, 2025 |title=Maryland Gov. Wes Moore to campaign for Spanberger in Northern Virginia Saturday |url=https://wjla.com/news/elections/maryland-gov-wes-moore-to-campaign-for-spanberger-in-northern-virginia-saturday-elections-governor-race-va-abigail-winsome-earle-sears-democrat-republican-ballot-early-voting |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251101041945/https://wjla.com/news/elections/maryland-gov-wes-moore-to-campaign-for-spanberger-in-northern-virginia-saturday-elections-governor-race-va-abigail-winsome-earle-sears-democrat-republican-ballot-early-voting |archive-date=November 1, 2025 |access-date=March 15, 2026 |website=ABC 7}} Obama and Spanberger held a high-profile rally in [[Norfolk, Virginia|Norfolk]] known as the "Virginia Votes Rally." Obama's speech focused on the economy, democracy, and Trump—most of Spanberger's advertisements continued to tie Earle-Sears to Trump.{{Cite web |last=Cox |first=Leila |date=November 2, 2025 |title=Spanberger, Obama rally brings thousands to Chartway Arena in Norfolk |url=https://www.13newsnow.com:443/article/news/politics/elections/spanberger-obama-rally-brings-thousands-to-chartway-arena/291-be64a36f-50b2-4487-9b71-efab624c2538 |archive-url=https://megalodon.jp/2026-0314-1041-15/https://www.13newsnow.com:443/article/news/politics/elections/spanberger-obama-rally-brings-thousands-to-chartway-arena/291-be64a36f-50b2-4487-9b71-efab624c2538 |archive-date=March 14, 2026 |access-date=March 14, 2026 |website=13 New Now}}{{Cite web |date=November 2, 2025 |title=WATCH: Obama rallies with Democratic candidates in Virginia and New Jersey |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/watch-live-obama-rallies-with-democratic-candidates-in-virginia-and-new-jersey |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260205073136/https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/watch-live-obama-rallies-with-democratic-candidates-in-virginia-and-new-jersey |archive-date=February 5, 2026 |access-date=March 13, 2026 |website=[[PBS]]}} Trump did not campaign with nor officially endorse Earle-Sears; however, he did support her over Spanberger.{{Cite web |last=Manchester |first=Julia |date=November 3, 2025 |title=Trump does not mention Earle-Sears by name in Virginia telephone rally |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5587472-trump-does-not-mention-earle-sears-rally/ |access-date=March 16, 2026 |website=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]}}{{Cite web |last=Daniels |first=Cheyanne M. |date=November 3, 2025 |title=Trump endorses dozens ahead of Tuesday elections — but doesn't name Earle-Sears |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/11/03/trump-endorses-republicans-earle-sears-00633218 |access-date=March 15, 2026 |website=[[Politico]]}} ===Debate=== Both Spanberger and Earle-Sears initially declined to debate. In August, they agreed to meet on October 9 at [[Norfolk State University]] for one televised debate.{{cite web | last=Woods | first=Charlotte Rene | title=Debating the debates: Spanberger, Earle-Sears to face off Oct. 9 | website=[[Virginia Mercury]] | date=August 18, 2025 | url=https://virginiamercury.com/2025/08/18/debating-the-debates-spanberger-earle-sears-to-face-off-oct-9/ | access-date=August 27, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250818215141/https://virginiamercury.com/2025/08/18/debating-the-debates-spanberger-earle-sears-to-face-off-oct-9/|archive-date=August 18, 2025}} Topics discussed during the debate included repeal of the car tax, political violence and rhetoric, the federal government shutdown, economic policies on data centers, affordability, transgender policies in schools, reproductive rights, immigration, education, and marijuana legalization.{{Cite web |title=Virginia governor nominees face-off in only debate before election day |website=WJLA.com |date=2025-10-09 |url=https://wjla.com/news/elections/gubernatorial-virginia-debate-winsome-earle-sears-abigail-spanberger-democrats-republicans-race-campaign-norfolk-state-hampton-roads-live-updates-october-voters-issues-education-politics-governor-polls-ckncern |access-date=2025-10-09 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251010003332/https://wjla.com/news/elections/gubernatorial-virginia-debate-winsome-earle-sears-abigail-spanberger-democrats-republicans-race-campaign-norfolk-state-hampton-roads-live-updates-october-voters-issues-education-politics-governor-polls-ckncern |archive-date=2025-10-10 }} Earle-Sears's debate style was described as "aggressive" as she frequently interrupted Spanberger. Spanberger sometimes "simply stood silent" and did not answer Earle-Sears's questions directed toward her. Earle-Sears made Jay Jones's messages and transgender policies a central part of her messaging.{{Cite web |last=Schneider |first=Gregory S. |last2=Cox |first2=Erin |date=October 10, 2025 |title=8 takeaways from the Spanberger and Earle-Sears debate in Virginia |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/dc-md-va/2025/10/10/virginia-governor-debate-earle-sears-spanberger/ |access-date=March 17, 2026 |website=[[The Washington Post]]}} Spanberger condemned Jones's text messages but did not call for him to withdraw from the race. She declined to state if she would renew her endorsement of Jones. Earle-Sears pressured Spanberger to call for Jones to withdraw from the race.{{Cite web |date=October 10, 2025 |title=Abigail Spanberger and Winsome Earle-Sears clash over Jay Jones' violent texts in lone Virginia governor's debate |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/elections/abigail-spanberger-winsome-earle-sears-virgina-governor-debate-rcna235418 |access-date=October 11, 2025 |website=[[NBC News]] |language=en|last=Edelman|first=Adam|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260118131624/https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/elections/abigail-spanberger-winsome-earle-sears-virgina-governor-debate-rcna235418|archive-date=January 18, 2026}} Both candidates attacked each other on political violence and rhetoric. On education, Earle-Sears called for policies that would ban transgender students from [[Bathroom bill|bathrooms]] and [[Transgender people in sports|sports]] which do not conform to their birth sex; Spanberger called for local control over transgender policies in schools.{{Cite web |last=Schmidt |first=Markus |date=October 9, 2025 |title=Spanberger, Earle-Sears clash over violence, abortion, and taxes in lone Va. governor's debate |url=https://virginiamercury.com/2025/10/09/spanberger-earle-sears-clash-over-violence-abortion-and-taxes-in-lone-va-governors-debate/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251010151242/https://virginiamercury.com/2025/10/09/spanberger-earle-sears-clash-over-violence-abortion-and-taxes-in-lone-va-governors-debate/ |archive-date=October 10, 2025 |access-date=March 28, 2026 |website=[[Virginia Mercury]]}} Both Earle-Sears and Spanberger called for bipartisan support to end the shutdown.{{Cite web |last=FOX 5 DC Digital Team |date=October 10, 2025 |title=Virginia Governor Debate: Candidates clash over shutdown, violent rhetoric |url=https://www.fox5dc.com/news/virginia-governor-debate-candidates-clash-over-shutdown-violent-rhetoric |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251010170829/https://www.fox5dc.com/news/virginia-governor-debate-candidates-clash-over-shutdown-violent-rhetoric |archive-date=October 10, 2025 |access-date=April 6, 2026 |website=[[Fox 5 DC]]}} Earle-Sears, who was not endorsed by Trump, stated, "I will take all endorsements, including the president." According to CNN, Spanberger "went on offense" when she said Earle-Sears previously opposed same-sex marriage; Earle-Sears responded by saying, "That's not discrimination."{{cite web |last1=Bradner |first1=Eric |date=October 9, 2025 |title=Takeaways from the only debate in the Virginia governor's race |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2025/10/09/politics/virginia-governor-debate-takeaways |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251010175909/https://edition.cnn.com/2025/10/09/politics/virginia-governor-debate-takeaways |archive-date=October 10, 2025 |access-date=April 7, 2026 |website=[[CNN]]}} ==== Analysis ==== Political analyst David Richards said Spanberger won the debate: "Earle-Sears' attempts to drag Spanberger into the Jay Jones scandal were unsuccessful. Overall, I'd give Spanberger a small edge because she seemed calmer and more professional." On their separate performances, Richards stated, "Spanberger held her own and came off as much more polished and capable, if not a little cold. Earle-Sears often came across as slightly unhinged." Spanberger's sizable victory was attributed to concerns over affordability, Earle-Sears' tendency to change staff and failure to find a convincing message, Spanberger's fundraising advantage, a significant decline in turnout in heavily Republican Southwest Virginia, and outrage in Northern Virginia over the mass layoffs of federal workers as part of President Donald Trump's efforts to downsize the [[Federal government of the United States|federal government]].{{Cite web|title=13 reasons why Spanberger and the Democrats won so big. Trump is just one of them.|url=https://cardinalnews.org/2025/11/05/13-reasons-why-spanberger-and-the-democrats-won-so-big-trump-is-just-one-of-them/|website=Cardinal News|date=2025-11-05|access-date=2026-02-01|language=en-US|first=Dwayne|last=Yancey}} Additionally, many furloughed federal workers were energized by the ongoing federal government shutdown. Discontentment with the [[Economy of the United States|U.S. economy]] under Trump, which many Virginians blamed on [[Tariffs in the second Trump administration|his tariff policies]], also played a factor in motivating Spanberger voters.{{cite news|last1=Flynn|first1=Meagan|last2=Cox|first2=Erin|title=Five takeaways from Virginia's general election|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/dc-md-va/2025/11/05/virginia-general-election-results-takeaways/|date=November 5, 2025|access-date=November 5, 2025|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|language=en}} The layoffs boosted Spanberger in [[Northern Virginia]] which contributed to her large victory margin.{{Cite news |last=Barthel |first=Margaret |date=November 4, 2025 |title=Democrat Spanberger wins Virginia governor race with message on DOGE, cost of living |url=https://www.npr.org/2025/11/04/nx-s1-5589144/election-results-virginia-governor-spanberger |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251105025530/https://www.npr.org/2025/11/04/nx-s1-5589144/election-results-virginia-governor-spanberger |archive-date=November 5, 2025 |access-date=December 7, 2025 |work=[[NPR News]]}} Northern Virginia backed 88% of her statewide margin, where every locality in the region saw her margin increase significantly from [[Terry McAuliffe|McAuliffe's]] performance in [[2021 Virginia gubernatorial election|2021]]. She could have won statewide without Northern Virginia by three points.{{Cite web|last=Potter|first=Bruce|date=November 5, 2025|title=Northern Virginia accounts for 88% of Spanberger's victory margin|url=https://wtop.com/virginia-election/2025/11/northern-virginia-accounts-for-88-of-spanbergers-victory-margin/|archive-url=https://megalodon.jp/2026-0516-0706-14/https://wtop.com:443/virginia-election/2025/11/northern-virginia-accounts-for-88-of-spanbergers-victory-margin/|archive-date=May 15, 2025|access-date=December 5, 2025|website=[[WTOP News]]}} Spanberger did well with college-educated voters, winning voters with college degrees by 27 points (63%-36%). Many college campuses shifted leftward by 18 points on average due to young voters. [[Virginia Tech]] shifted 34 points to the left, which was the largest shift of all the college campuses. Spanberger's strongest independent city was [[Charlottesville, Virginia|Charlottesville]], where the [[University of Virginia]], her [[alma mater]], is located. The evangelical [[Liberty University]] in [[Lynchburg, Virginia|Lynchburg]] shifted to the left by six points.{{Cite news |last=Kutner |first=Brad |date=December 2, 2025 |title=Virginia's 2025 election certified, colleges swung hard left |url=https://www.wvtf.org/news/2025-12-02/virginias-2025-election-certified-colleges-swung-hard-left |access-date=December 7, 2025 |work=[[RadioIQ]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260128001008/https://www.wvtf.org/news/2025-12-02/virginias-2025-election-certified-colleges-swung-hard-left|archive-date=January 28, 2026}} College-educated voters made up more of the electorate compared to [[2021 Virginia gubernatorial election|2021]]. Spanberger narrowly won non-college-educated voters (50%-49%) despite Youngkin's 19-point margin (59%-40%) with non-college-educated voters from 2021.{{Cite web |date=November 3, 2021 |title="Exit polls for Election Results 2021 {{!}} CNN Politics" |url=https://www.cnn.com/election/2021/november/exit-polls/virginia/general/governor/0 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251118112530/https://www.cnn.com/election/2021/november/exit-polls/virginia/general/governor/0 |archive-date=November 18, 2025 |access-date=January 15, 2026 |website=[[CNN]]}} This is the first time since [[1985 Virginia gubernatorial election|1985]] that a Democrat carried [[Spotsylvania County, Virginia|Spotsylvania County]], a notable Republican stronghold, as well as [[Waynesboro, Virginia|Waynesboro City]]. [[Stafford County, Virginia|Stafford County]] also flipped for the first time since 1985, though Harris won Stafford in [[2024 United States presidential election in Virginia|2024]]. [[Nelson County, Virginia|Nelson County]] and [[Caroline County, Virginia|Caroline County]] also voted Democratic for the first time since [[2013 Virginia gubernatorial election|2013]]. [[James City County, Virginia|James City County]] voted Democratic for the first time since [[2005 Virginia gubernatorial election|2005]], although it voted Democratic in 2020 and 2024.{{Cite web |last1=Yancey|first1=Dwayne|date=November 7, 2025|title=Virginia's blue wave was real but not as big as it looked. Here are the numbers.|url=https://cardinalnews.org/2025/11/07/virginias-blue-wave-was-real-but-not-as-big-as-it-looked-here-are-the-numbers/|access-date=November 7, 2025|website=Cardinal News|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251107180817/https://cardinalnews.org/2025/11/07/virginias-blue-wave-was-real-but-not-as-big-as-it-looked-here-are-the-numbers/|archive-date=November 7, 2025}} Spanberger's closest victory was in [[York County, Virginia|York County]], which voted Democratic for the first time since [[1965 Virginia gubernatorial election|1965]].{{cite web|url=http://uselectionatlas.org/RESULTS|title=Dave Leip's Atlas of U.S. Presidential Elections|first=David|last=Leip|website=uselectionatlas.org|access-date=November 9, 2025}} Spanberger improved with Latino voters from [[2024 United States presidential election in Virginia|2024]].{{Cite news |last=Manzanares |first=Keyris |date=November 25, 2024 |title=How Virginia's Latinos voted in the 2024 election |url=https://www.whro.org/elections/2024-11-25/how-virginias-latinos-voted-in-the-2024-election |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250518235653/https://www.whro.org/elections/2024-11-25/how-virginias-latinos-voted-in-the-2024-election |archive-date=May 18, 2025 |access-date=December 7, 2025 |work=WHRO Public Media}} === Exit poll === {| class="wikitable sortable" style="font-size:90%; line-height:1.2" |+ 2025 Virginia gubernatorial election voter demographics (CNN){{Cite web |title=Exit polls for Election Results 2025 {{!}} CNN Politics |url=https://www.cnn.com/election/2025/exit-polls/virginia/general/governor/0 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251116220548/https://www.cnn.com/election/2025/exit-polls/virginia/general/governor/0 |archive-date=November 16, 2025 |access-date=November 6, 2025 |website=[[CNN]]}} |- !
